what: A full-screen video (or canvas or photo) is covered with a Gaussian blur (σ6, .4 resolution, taps 3+2σ) and a .6 veil of the background color, and only where the cursor passes is it wiped clear — a point following the cursor with .4s power3 paints a segment of width .2 (thinning to .12 the faster it moves, inner 40% solid) from the previous spot to the current spot onto a half-resolution plate, and the plate fades out over 1 second. Stroke edges refract slightly toward the alpha gradient. When the source changes, a ring band rippling in six lobes spreads from the center over .85s power1.inOut as it switches (wave refraction near the band + color bleed 3), and a sharp focus ring, only between it and a second circle trailing .05s behind, passes once.

options.veil: Background color overlay, default .6 (original touch · low-power .675)
options.aberration: Color fringing strength on the way out, default 3 — 0 turns it off
options.trail: At 0 the cursor trail is off (always off on touch devices and reduced motion)
options.source: Initial source CSS selector (if none, waits for fx:source)
options.look: If local, inside the wrapping section instead of fixed to the screen (position:absolute)

use: · Fire: el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('fx:source', { detail: { el: videoOrCanvas } }))

from.where: shared.js .gb-bg (the plate behind every page) — original Background (BM3SHlsX): GaussianBlurNode σ6, resolutionScale .4, veil .6, aberration 3, brush stroke F .5 resolution, width I .2, thinness L .6, speed z .65, fade-out R 1, fade-in V .5, refocus unblur (.85−.05) and reblur (.85, .05 later) power1.inOut, video grind progress .85 power1.inOut (BAQjCura ripple circle T .06, E .04, D .06, O .012)

note: The original was built with three WebGPU and TSL nodes — the same values were rewritten in WebGL GLSL. The canvas source is re-uploaded for each Frame. The plate is not drawn when off screen
